correctness.rationale: For every sign word, the exact coefficient score is computed by transition counts. Strict comparisons show only the alternating word (odd n) or its two orientations (even n) maximize the moment sum at all positive tilts. The entropy variational inequality identifies exact minimizing histograms. A maximal-span lattice local central limit theorem after exponential tilting produces the stated full tail coefficient, and nonmaximizing words are exponentially negligible. The endpoint identity equals 2 minus endpoint masses and adjacent minima, giving an independent-set count. The packaged checker verified 8,212 exact rational sign comparisons, 75,498 finite histogram configurations, and 12 binomial-tail asymptotic comparisons. No numerical experiment is used as proof of an infinite result.

value.rationale: Ordered-histogram DTV is designed for comb-like departures and exact false-positive calibration matters when N grows. The theorem resolves its natural proportional-tail question with a fully explicit noncentral sharp exponent, parity-dependent rare-event minimizers, lattice oscillations, and maximum-threshold rate. Its all-n alternating dominance lemma and conditional profile give structural information not available from an expectation or black-box dynamic-programming evaluation. It does not claim a general new large-deviation principle; the specific optimal profile and finite-size coefficient are the mathematical value.
